page.layout: Two medallion portraits with legends at the top, centred; below them one column of running text with two paragraphs. The running head sits at the top, the page number at the top left.

main_text.p: TARQVINIVS Priscus qui prius Lucumo, Romanorum rex quintus, imperauit Romanis anno mundi 3349. ante Christum natum 613. apud Ancum Martium liberaliter dextréque obeundo officia, in familiarem venit amicitiam, vt publicis ac priuatis consiliis bello,domíque interesset, & per omnia expertus postremo tutor etiam liberis Regis, testamento instituieretur.mortuo Anco, instituit hic vt quàm primum comitia Regi creando fierent,quibus indictis,sub tempus pueros regios venatum ablegauit:& primus petiffe ambitiosè regnum & orationem habuiffe ad conciliandos plebis animos compositam fertur:maximè verò cùm Tatium Sabinum,etiam ex hoste Regem factum diceret,ac inculcaret,populus eum regnare iuffit. numerum Senatorum & equitū duplicauit: Circum Romae aedificauit, ludos Romanos instituit magnificos: Sabinos vicit: Latinos priscos domuit: primus triumphans Romae intrauit:muros & cloacas fecit: Capitolium inchoauit. Tandem à filiis Anci Martij, cui in regno succesferat, interfectus est 37. imperij anno. his temporibus Ierusalem à Nabuchodonosore capta ac euersa est:& Massilia condita. Consulito lib.1.Eutrop. Diony.Halicar.lib.3. Titum Liuium lib.1.deca.1.

TANAQVIL, Tarquinij Prisci vxor fuit, perita, vt vulgo Etrusci, coelestium prodigiorum mulier. Hæc cùm aquila suspensis demissa leniter alis pileum viri abstuliffet, rursúsque velut ministerio diuinitus missa, capiti aptè repofuiffet, hæc inquam, virum complexa,alta sperare iuffit. id siquidè factum est ipsis primò Romam ingredientibus,antequam regnaret ipse Tarquinius Priscus. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: The two medallion portraits are illustrations, not text. Their legends are set in the coin rims and are only partly legible: the left medallion shows a bearded figure with legend fragments reading "TARQVINIVS PRI" and "CVS"; the right medallion shows a female bust with legend "TANAQVIL" and "TARQVIN". The exact letters at the rim edges are uncertain and are marked [?]. No marginal notes, catchword or signature are printed on this page.
